thesis: Modal voltron with a wheel finisher: land either commander and let it tax every card that moves (Shabraz a counter and a life per draw, Brallin a counter and a ping per discard), keep it fed with steady draw and loots and multiplied by the doublers, then win by 21 commander damage or by a wheel cashed against a second collector, with v2.3.0's Treasure loop off the table's draws still a candidate.

stages.label: PAY FOR A COMMANDER, THEN FOR THE TURN
stages.what_it_does: 36 lands and eight rocks (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Azorius and Izzet Signets, both Talismans, Mind Stone, Thought Vessel) pay for a 4- or 5-mana commander, then for a wheel or a draw spell cast with X on the same turn. The nine-card ramp group (the eight rocks plus Smothering Tithe) is in 49.8% of opening sevens and drawn by turn six in 80.8% (deck-audit). deck-facts: land sources R 31 / U 28 / W 22 against targets R 36 / U 36 / W 22, and 13 lands can enter tapped. v2.3.0 adds a Treasure wing that the table's draws pay for: Tithe (a Treasure per opponent draw they do not pay 2 for), Xorn (one extra Treasure per batch) and Zirda (activated abilities cost 2 less, never below one mana, so Gleaming Splendor's draw costs {W}, Faerie Mastermind's {1}{U}, and Shark Typhoon's cycling and Magus of the Wheel get cheaper). Six Commander Spellbook lines built from Tithe with Splendor or Mastermind plus Zirda, Xorn, Bard or Mirrormade are candidates only (needs a stack scenario): each assumes opponents decline Tithe's {2}. Thought Vessel is filed here for its mana, but its other line (no maximum hand size) switches off the cleanup discard that ends stack 009, so it is a card the wheel kill wants off the table (open_questions[0]). Lands with a second job: Raugrin Triome cycles and Otawara channels (both a discard, so Brallin pays, by oracle text), and Fiery Islet sacrifices for a draw (Shabraz pays).

evidence.note: all nine of its 99 members are here; of ramp:treasure's three only Smothering Tithe is (Gleaming Splendor is in fuel, Prismari Command in protection); ramp:cost-reduction's one, Zirda, is here

15 of 47 in Ramp (15 cards, all of it): Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Mind Stone, Thought Vessel, Smothering Tithe, the four fetches, the any-colour lands

stages.label: A COMMANDER ON THE BATTLEFIELD
stages.what_it_does: Nothing in the commander half pays until Shabraz (5 mana, flying) or Brallin (4 mana) has resolved and survived. Shabraz turns each card you draw into a +1/+1 counter and 1 life; Brallin turns each card you discard into a +1/+1 counter and 1 damage to each opponent (stack 007: Kitsa's one-card loot is one counter and one ping). The deck is modal, so the ignition is redundant rather than single: either commander can be the 21-damage threat, both start in the command zone, and the constraint is casting and keeping one, never drawing it. The pilot's rule since game 004 is to cast the first commander on curve and hold wheels until one is out (CONTEXT). The brief prices no commander-cast rate; it prices the cover, the six-card protection group, drawn by turn six in 68.3% (deck-audit), which says drawn, not used at the right moment. The ignition is not the only start: stacks 011 and 013 resolve Wheel of Fortune under Razorkin Needlehead with both commanders in the command zone (21 per seat under Torbran, 14 under Gratuitous Violence), so the draw-side collector runs without a commander. goldfish_targets still names a WHEEL as the ignition and marks it required; this model reads a wheel as the finisher the commander waits for (proposed_goldfish_edits[0]).

evidence.note: Brallin out, Kitsa loots one card: one Brallin trigger, a counter and a ping to each opponent; every non-basic card on its board is in the 99 (basics are counted as mana, see notes[0])

Brallin and Needlehead under one Wheel of Fortune: three discards are three Brallin triggers (6/6); the opponents' draws pay Needlehead separately, 7 per seat; every non-basic card on its board is in the 99 (basics are counted as mana, see notes[0])
the commander-free exception: Wheel of Fortune under Needlehead and Torbran, 21 per seat with both commanders in the command zone

stages.label: STEADY DRAW BETWEEN WHEELS
stages.what_it_does: What v2.3.0 was built to fix: the deck spent cards faster than it replaced them (CONTEXT, game 006). Three groups keep a commander paid without emptying the hand. LOOTS pay both commanders at once (a draw for Shabraz, a discard for Brallin): Kitsa ({T}), Teferi, Master of Time (+1 at instant speed), Faithless Looting, Cathartic Reunion (two discards, three draws), and Shark Typhoon's instant-speed cycling, which also leaves an X/X flying Shark. Rielle draws as many as you discard, the first time each turn. MANA INTO CARDS with no discard: Mind Spring (X), Rush of Knowledge (the greatest mana value you control; Sphinx, Bard, Fiery Emancipation and a cast Typhoon are 6), and Prosperity (X for every player, so it pays Needlehead, Sphinx and Tithe on the opponents' draws, and with none out it only feeds the table). STANDING ENGINES: Rhystic Study, Faerie Mastermind (flash; {3}{U} makes every player draw) and Gleaming Splendor ({2}{W}: two target players draw, plus a Treasure on an opponent's second draw each turn). Idyllic Tutor finds an enchantment; it finds no wheel. The six-card standing-draw group is drawn by turn six in 66.1%; the discard-converter group (Mako, Rielle, Typhoon) in 44.5% (deck-audit). There is no separate fodder stage: the resource a discard consumes is the deck's own hand, and every card in it is fodder for Brallin. Psychosis Crawler is a creature that drains on each of these draws (output).

evidence.note: Kitsa's loot resolves and its discard triggers Brallin; every non-basic card on its board is in the 99 (basics are counted as mana, see notes[0])

Shark Typhoon cycled for X=4 pays Brallin, Mako and Shabraz and leaves a flying Shark; its board names Sundown Pass (cut in draw-engine-v1) among the lands that paid, and the 4/4 is a ruling-based input, so this is the shape on the 99, not a citable proof

stages.label: MAKE EACH CARD WORTH MORE
stages.what_it_does: The commanders turn one card into one counter or one ping; these eight raise what each card is worth. DAMAGE: Torbran adds 2 to each damage event from a red source to an opponent; Gratuitous Violence doubles damage from your creatures; Fiery Emancipation triples damage from any source you control. With all three out one Brallin ping is 8, 10, 12 or 18 per opponent and each opponent orders the replacements, so 8 if they minimise (stack 007). On Needlehead's draw pings Torbran makes each 3 (stack 011: 21 per seat) and Gratuitous Violence each 2 (stack 013: 14 per seat). Brallin is red, so Torbran counts on his commander damage; Shabraz is white-blue, so only the two multipliers do (oracle text). None of them touches Psychosis Crawler, which causes life loss, not damage. COUNTERS: Lae'zel adds one to every counter placement, so each draw and each discard is two counters; it is a single card, drawn by turn six in 17.8% (deck-audit, a named single point of failure). DRAWS: Bard and Teferi's Ageless Insight turn each draw after your first draw-step draw into two; Consecrated Sphinx draws two per opponent draw, so a draw-seven wheel is 21 Sphinx triggers (stack 009); Windfall, Jace's Archivist and Incendiary Command give as many as the opponents draw. Mirrormade is a second copy of whichever artifact or enchantment is out: a multiplier, Smothering Tithe or Rhystic Study, so it is only as good as the table. The three-card amplifier group is in 19.9% of openers and drawn by turn six in 43.9% (deck-audit).

stages.label: THE SECOND COLLECTORS
stages.what_it_does: Creatures that collect a second tax on the same cards the commanders tax. Razorkin Needlehead deals 1 to an opponent for each card that opponent draws, so the three draw-seven wheels (Wheel of Fortune, Reforge the Soul, Magus of the Wheel) pay it seven per seat whatever your hand held; Windfall and Jace's Archivist pay the largest hand discarded, and Incendiary Command each opponent's own discard, possibly 0: stack 014 resolves one Wheel of Fortune under Brallin and Needlehead as 3 discard pings plus 7 draw pings, 10 per seat (Brallin 6/6). Psychosis Crawler (new in v2.3.0) makes each opponent lose 1 life per card you draw, so every draw that feeds Shabraz also drains the table; it is life loss, so no amplifier in the deck touches it, and its size is your hand. Glint-Horn Buccaneer deals 1 to each opponent per card you discard, a second Brallin, with haste and a {1}{R} loot while attacking. Marauding Mako takes a counter per card discarded and cycles. The wheel-kill damage component (Glint-Horn, Crawler, Needlehead) is three cards in 19.9% of openers; paired with a wheel it is drawn by turn six in 38.2%, mean turn 6.144 (deck-audit). Glint-Horn alone is a named single point of failure for its target, drawn by turn six in 17.6%. Six wheels make the opponents draw, plus Collective Defiance aimed at one opponent; Needlehead earns nothing from the five that wheel only your hand. No passing stack has Glint-Horn or Crawler on the battlefield.

stages.label: KEEP THE COMMANDER, CLEAR THE LANE
stages.what_it_does: The engine is a creature that one removal spell answers, and each removal adds 2 to that commander's tax. Constant cover: Lightning Greaves (shroud and haste, equip 0). Held cover: Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat (both free with a commander out), Loran's Escape (hexproof and indestructible), and the counters Negate and Stubborn Denial (a hard counter once a creature has power 4, which a grown commander does). Grand Abolisher stops the table casting spells or activating artifact, creature and enchantment abilities on your turn, which is the turn the wheel or the double-strike attack happens. Answers that clear a blocker or a hate piece: Swords to Plowshares, Get Lost, Chaos Warp, Prismari Command (two damage, a loot, a Treasure or an artifact kill, two of them). The six-card protection group is drawn by turn six in 68.3% and the seven-card answers group in 72.9% (deck-audit); both price drawing a card, never holding it for the right moment. Akroma's Will protects too, filed under wincon because its double strike is the kill. Otawara, a land, channels to bounce a threat (mana). Nothing here counters a creature spell. No passing stack resolves any of these protecting a commander; stacks 014 and 008 hold Negate and Swords only as cards discarded to a wheel.

stages.label: TWENTY-ONE, OR THE WHEEL
stages.what_it_does: Two endings, chosen each game. COMMANDER DAMAGE: a grown commander connects for 21. Double strike comes from Blade Historian (every attacker) or Akroma's Will (flying, vigilance and double strike, plus indestructible and protection with a commander out); Brotherhood Regalia makes it unblockable with ward 2 (equip {1} on a legend). Shu Yun and Embercleave are gone, so two double-strike sources remain and no passing stack resolves either (open_questions[2]). THE WHEEL: twelve full-hand discard-and-draws, cast with a commander out. Six make every player draw (Wheel of Fortune, Windfall, Reforge the Soul, Magus of the Wheel, Jace's Archivist, Incendiary Command), which is what pays Needlehead, Sphinx, Tithe and Splendor; Collective Defiance wheels one target player; five wheel only your hand (Tolarian Winds, Shattered Perception, Heartwarming Redemption, Borrowed Knowledge, Fateful Showdown). Eleven discard your own hand and pay Brallin with what you hold; Collective Defiance does only if you target yourself, and then no opponent draws. The wheel group is in 60.7% of opening sevens and drawn by turn six in 87.3%, mean turn 2.533 (deck-audit), so the job is holding one, not finding one. Of the 14 passing stacks two end a game: 009, Wheel of Fortune under Consecrated Sphinx with both commanders out, the only one that kills all three seats, its last step the cleanup discard firing Brallin 42 times (with Thought Vessel out that discard does not happen, open_questions[0]); and 006, one seat to 21 commander damage, through the cut Fireshrieker. Every other wheel line on file is short of 40 per seat: 21 (011), 14 (013), 10 (014).

One ping under all three replacements: 8, 10, 12 or 18 per opponent, each opponent choosing the order; 8 if they minimise (40 to 32).
The wheel taxed on the draw side: seven Needlehead triggers per opponent, 3 each under Torbran, 21 per seat (40 to 19). No commander on the board. Not a kill.
The same wheel under Gratuitous Violence: each trigger 2, 14 per seat (40 to 26). Not a kill.
The wheel's discard pays the commander: the three cards in hand when Wheel of Fortune resolves are three Brallin triggers, 3 per seat, Brallin 6/6. The discard half is the hand held minus the wheel.

The same wheel's opponent draws pay Needlehead independently: seven triggers per seat, 7 per seat, reported in 014 as a separate tally from Brallin's (together 10 per seat, 40 to 30). Neither collector causes the other's trigger; 011 and 013 show the Needlehead half with no commander out.

THE POD KILL ON FILE. 49 cards drawn (7 + 21 Sphinx triggers x 2), Shabraz 52/52, the cleanup discard of 42 fires Brallin and all three opponents reach 0 after the 40th trigger. Verified on the board 009 resolved, whose only off-list card is a basic Island (notes[0]'s rule: basics are mana). That board has no Thought Vessel, and 009's extras say nothing changes your maximum hand size: with Vessel out (v2.3.0) there is no cleanup discard and this line stops at Shabraz 52/52 (open_questions[0]).

A cycle pays both commanders: the cost discard triggers Brallin, the draw triggers Shabraz, and the cycle trigger makes a flying Shark Brallin can give trample. Stack 012 passed on this shape, but its board pays with Sundown Pass (cut) and names Shark Typhoon only in stack prose, so it does not verify the line on the 99.

Kitsa copies the wheel: stack 010 passed with 10 discards, 14 draws, 10 per seat, Brallin 13/13, Shabraz 17/17. Null because 010's hand names Boros Charm (cut), one of the three cards discarded; the count would hold with any card of the 99 in its place, which a re-run would show.
Lae'zel doubles each commander trigger's counter: stack 008 passed (Windfall, five discards and seven draws: Brallin 13/13, Shabraz 17/17, 5 per seat). Null because 008's hand names Silence (cut).

The modal voltron kill: a grown commander with double strike connects for 21. Claim only: the one stack with this arithmetic (006) used Fireshrieker, cut, and no passing stack resolves combat with Blade Historian or Akroma's Will (open_questions[2]).
By oracle text: under the 009 board, 49 draws would be 49 life lost by each opponent from Crawler, a kill that does not need the cleanup discard Thought Vessel removes. No stack (open_questions[1]).

The Treasure loop the pilot called the contender (CONTEXT, 2026-11-04): Splendor's draw at {W} under Zirda makes opponents draw, Tithe and Splendor make Treasure off those draws, the Treasure pays the next activation. A Commander Spellbook candidate, needs a stack scenario; each opponent may pay {2} to deny Tithe's Treasure (open_questions[3]).
By oracle text, Prosperity for X is X Needlehead pings per opponent and X draws for Shabraz; without a draw-side payoff out it only refills the table. No stack.

Both halves under Torbran from an eight-card hand (Wheel plus seven): 21 from Brallin's seven discards plus 21 from Needlehead's seven draws would be 42 per seat from 40. 014 sums the halves on one board without Torbran (10), 011 prices Needlehead's half under Torbran (21); no stack holds all four (open_questions[4]).

map_disagreements.why: The map files a wheel by what else it is: the eight spells whose only job is the wheel sit in Card Flow; Magus and Jace's Archivist, creatures with tap abilities, and the two modal Commands whose other modes deal damage sit in Bodies. To the engine all twelve are one finisher, because a discard pays Brallin and a draw pays Shabraz whatever else the card says. The split the engine does care about, symmetrical (six) against one-sided (five), is invisible to the map: it puts Wheel of Fortune beside Tolarian Winds, but only one of the two pays Needlehead, Sphinx or Tithe.

The multipliers are replacement effects whose text names damage, counters or draws, and the map clusters on those nouns: the damage enchantments and Torbran with the Finishers, Bard and Lae'zel with the commanders in Payoffs, Teferi's Ageless Insight and Mirrormade with the draw spells, Consecrated Sphinx with the creatures. What unites them, multiplying a commander trigger, is a relation to Brallin and Shabraz no single card's text states.

Card Flow holds the draw spells and loots (8 of 13), but the repeatable loots and Splendor (Kitsa, Teferi, Master of Time, Gleaming Splendor) sit in Payoffs with the commanders, Faerie Mastermind with the creatures, and Rielle with the Finishers. They do one job here, paying both commanders between wheels; the map reads their permanence, not their payment.

Insurance holds five of eleven; Lightning Greaves and Grand Abolisher land with the Finishers (equipment and a your-turn lock read as attack enablers), Deflecting Swat, Get Lost and Prismari Command with Bodies, Chaos Warp with Card Flow (it reveals off the top of a library). The engine reads them all as the same job: the commander survives the turn it matters.

The map splits the mana by its text, not its job: Ramp holds the any-colour lands, the fetches, the colourless rocks and Smothering Tithe; Mana holds the two-colour duals beside both Signets and both Talismans; and Xorn and Zirda sit with the Finishers. Xorn and Zirda are the new Treasure engine's multiplier and cost-cutter, the half of the Spellbook loops that is not Tithe, and nothing in their text says Tithe.

Against the v2.2.0 model's citations the v2.3.0 map relabelled its cities (Card Flow, Bodies, Finishers, Ramp, Mana, Insurance, Payoffs). Two labels describe their members loosely: Finishers (city-2) holds Rielle, Xorn, Zirda, Lightning Greaves and Grand Abolisher beside the damage enchantments, and Bodies (city-1) holds Get Lost, Deflecting Swat and both Commands. This model cites the labels as printed; the mismatch is a finding about the labeller, not the deck.

notes: Rebuilt for v2.3.0 (draw-engine-v1 merged 2026-11-05). ONE RULE for stacks against the 99: a stack verifies a line on this list when every NON-BASIC card its scenario names (board, hand, graveyard, stack) is in the 99. Basic lands are counted as mana, not as cards: 007 names three Mountains and 008 two where the 99 holds one, 009 taps an Island the 99 does not run, and in none does anything read a basic's identity. Under that rule 007, 009, 011, 013 and 014 are cited as verified_by. Not citable, each for a non-basic card: 001 holds Library of Leng, Sticky Fingers and Treasure Map in hand; 008 Silence; 010 Boros Charm; 012 pays with Sundown Pass; 002 and 003 have Library of Leng on the battlefield; 004 Magmakin Artillerist and Artist's Talent; 005 Spider-Man and Swiftfoot Boots; 006 Fireshrieker. Those are cited, where at all, only as shape. Proposed check: expand_copies over every card a cited stack names against the decklist, with basics reported but not failed.
No fodder stage: the deck consumes its own hand, so there is no card whose job is to be eaten.

engine-facts' declared_engines (the strategic frame's prose) still names Artist's Talent, Magmakin Artillerist, Shu Yun, Embercleave, Robe of Stars and March of Swirling Mist, all cut; the frame is stale against the 99 and disagrees with this model.

findings.claim: ignition -> output via Brallin, Razorkin Needlehead, Wheel of Fortune, verified_by 014: 'Both halves of one wheel ... three discards are three Brallin pings, seven opponent draws are seven Needlehead pings, 10 per seat'
findings.note: Stack 014 establishes that two collectors tax ONE wheel in parallel, not that anything moves from the ignition stage to the output stage. Its step 2 fires Brallin on YOUR three discards; its step 3 fires Needlehead on the OPPONENTS' 21 draws; final_state reports them as separate tallies (damage_from_brallin 3, damage_from_needlehead 7). Neither trigger event is caused by the other card: stacks 011 and 013 resolve the same Wheel with the same opponent hands and give Needlehead exactly 7 triggers per seat with no commander on the board, so removing Brallin changes nothing on the Needlehead side. The note itself says 'both halves of one wheel', which describes a common SOURCE (wincon: Wheel of Fortune), not a flow. What 014 does support, each on its own: wincon -> ignition (the wheel's discard pays Brallin, 3 triggers, 6/6) and wincon -> output (the wheel's opponent draws pay Needlehead, 7 per seat). Not string-checkable, but a warning-level aid is: a verified line whose via includes a card placed in NEITHER its from nor its to stage (here Wheel of Fortune, wincon) is a line whose real source may be that third stage; surface it to the critic, do not gate on it (it also fires on lines[2]/[3], which are sound).

findings.claim: Every card on 007's board is in the 99.
findings.note: Stack 007's scenario lists 'Mountain' twice on the board and a third Mountain in the graveyard (discarded by Kitsa); decklist.txt holds '1 Mountain'. The same false sentence is in stages[1].evidence[0], stages[2].evidence[0] ('every board card in the 99'), stages[3].evidence[0] and notes[0] ('007, 011, 013 and 014 name only cards still in the deck'). The flow itself (Kitsa's one discard -> one Brallin trigger) is established by 007 steps 1-3 and the extra Mountains are irrelevant to it (mana_available {0}, nothing reads them). But that is exactly the situation of stack 009, which this model refuses to cite because its board taps 'a basic Island the 99 does not hold'. The rule is applied inconsistently: either an irrelevant off-list mana source disqualifies a stack (then 007 is shape too and lines[0]/[1] go dashed) or it does not (then 009's Island alone does not disqualify it, and lines[5] rests only on the Thought Vessel argument, which stands on its own). Pick one and apply it to both. Mechanically checkable, and should become a check: expand_copies over every card named in a cited stack's scenario (board, hand, graveyard, stack) against the decklist's copies would have flagged 007 (3 Mountains vs 1), 008 (2 Mountains, plus Silence), 009 (Island) and 012 (Sundown Pass) with no reading.

findings.claim: ignition -> conversion: one Brallin ping under Torbran, Gratuitous Violence and Fiery Emancipation is 8, 10, 12 or 18 per opponent; 8 if they minimise (40 to 32). verified_by 007
findings.note: 007 steps 3-8: Brallin (red creature, the source per 608.2h) deals 1; each opponent orders the three replacements (616.1), totals 8/10/12/18, minimised 8, 40 -> 32 per seat. The ping does flow into the multipliers. Figures match final_state exactly. Subject to the 007 copy-count inconsistency in lines[0].note.

findings.claim: fuel -> ignition: Kitsa's loot resolves, its one discard triggers Brallin, one counter and a ping. verified_by 007
findings.note: 007 step 1 resolves Kitsa's {T} loot (one discard, Mountain to the graveyard) and Brallin triggers exactly once; steps 2-3 put one counter on Brallin (4/4) and deal the ping. A fuel card paying a commander is what resolved. (The note's 'every card in the 99' sentence is the separate finding above.)

findings.claim: output -> conversion: Needlehead under Torbran, seven triggers per opponent, 3 each, 21 per seat (40 to 19), no commander on the board, not a kill. verified_by 011
findings.note: 011 steps 3 and 6: 7 Needlehead triggers per opponent, Torbran replaces each 1 with 3 (Needlehead is red), 40 -> 19; both commanders in the command zone. Every card on 011's board is in the 99 (one Mountain). Needlehead's damage does pass through Torbran. Direction note only: the stage order puts output after conversion, so this renders as a backward (feedback) arc; the stack shows a modifier acting on output's damage, not output returning a resource to conversion. Consistent with lines[1]'s source->multiplier convention, so not a defect, but the engineer may want the arrow to read conversion -> output.

findings.claim: output -> conversion: Needlehead under Gratuitous Violence, 2 each, 14 per seat (40 to 26). verified_by 013
findings.note: 013 step 6 establishes that GV doubles Needlehead's triggered damage because the creature is the source; 7 x 2 = 14, 40 -> 26 in final_state. Board is on the 99. Same direction remark as lines[2].

findings.claim: The only passing kill is Wheel of Fortune under Consecrated Sphinx with both commanders out (stack 009)
findings.note: Enumerated the 14 stacks: 006 (Shabraz + Kitsa, 21 between strikes) passes and ends with the opponent losing to 21 commander damage (final_state: '40 -> 30 -> 19 ... makes them lose the game'). It is a one-seat kill on a cut card (Fireshrieker), but it is a passing kill, and lines[9]'s own note cites it as 'the one stack with this arithmetic'. 009 is likewise off the 99 (Island), so the scoping that would make 'only' true ('the only passing POD kill' or 'the only passing kill of all three seats') must be stated. Same superlative in proposed_goldfish_edits[4].why ('Stack 009 is the only passing kill').

findings.claim: Razorkin Needlehead ... so a symmetrical wheel pays it seven per seat whatever your own hand held
findings.note: True of 3 of the 6 symmetrical wheels the same paragraph names (Wheel of Fortune, Reforge the Soul, Magus of the Wheel: 'draws seven'). By cards.json oracle text: Windfall and Jace's Archivist draw 'equal to the greatest number of cards a player discarded' (depends on every hand, yours included, and can be less or more than 7); Incendiary Command's mode has 'each player discards ... then draws that many cards', so each opponent draws their OWN discard count and an empty-handed opponent pays Needlehead 0. Stack 011 proves 7 for Wheel of Fortune only. The same generalisation is in stages[3].what_it_does ('one symmetrical wheel is 21 Sphinx triggers'), which also holds only for the draw-seven wheels.

findings.claim: Every one discards, so every one pays Brallin with the hand you hold.
findings.note: Collective Defiance's wheel mode is 'Target player discards all the cards in their hand' (cards.json); the same paragraph files it as wheeling 'one target player', and lines/stages[4] count it as a symmetrical-side card 'aimed at one opponent'. Aimed at an opponent it discards nothing of yours and pays Brallin 0; aimed at you it pays Brallin but no opponent draws. It cannot be both in one cast. Scope the sentence to eleven, or say 'or the opponent's'.

findings.claim: Sphinx + Wheel + both commanders, the kill on file, dashed: 009's Island and Thought Vessel
findings.note: Figures match 009's final_state (49 drawn = 7 + 21 x 2, Shabraz 52/52, cleanup discard of 42, all three at 0 after the 40th trigger). 009's extras state 'You have no effect that changes your maximum hand size', and Thought Vessel's oracle text is 'You have no maximum hand size', so the dashed status is honest on the Vessel ground alone, independent of the Island (see lines[0].note for the Island/Mountain consistency).

findings.claim: A cycle pays both commanders (Shark Typhoon); 012 passed on this shape but pays with Sundown Pass
findings.note: Dashed and honest. The note is phrased as fact, but the fact is exactly what 012 resolved (Brallin and Mako on the cost discard, the cycle trigger, then the draw for Shabraz; Brallin's '{R}: Target Shark gains trample' on the token), and the only off-list card is a tapped land used for mana. Whether that disqualifies is the same rule question raised in lines[0].note; whichever answer the engineer picks for 007/009 should be applied here too.

findings.claim: Kitsa copies the wheel; 010: 10 discards, 14 draws, 10 per seat, Brallin 13/13, Shabraz 17/17; 'the count would hold with any card of the 99 in its place'
